claims.claim: Account books, records and other documents related to running the business (including bank statements and reconciliation reports) must be kept for 7 years. claims.claim: Standing orders (הוראות קבע) are the most common recurring Israeli bank debit, and post-dated/deferred checks (שיקים דחויים) clear only on their future date and so stay reconciling items separate from ordinary outstanding checks. Both concepts derive from standard Israeli bookkeeping and receipt-recording practice.

claims.claim: At an 18% VAT rate the VAT portion of a VAT-INCLUSIVE amount is 18/118, i.e. about 15.25% (15.25%) of the gross. So a systematic gap of about 18% against a net figure, or about 15.25% against a gross figure, indicates a VAT-inclusive versus VAT-exclusive mismatch rather than a genuine reconciling item. This is arithmetic derived from the 18% rate, not a separate published figure.

claims.claim: Bank of Israel representative exchange rates are calculated once a day on foreign-currency business days only, so no rate is published on Saturdays, Sundays, Israeli holidays and certain other days. The rate is published after the afternoon sampling window closes, and the Bank of Israel states the rates have no official or legal standing in themselves.

claims.claim: Under the banking directives on the timing of credit and debit for cheques, the collecting bank credits the customer on the clearing day itself, and that credit becomes final only after three further business days, during which the drawee bank may still refuse the cheque.

claims.claim: Since 1 June 2026 a tax invoice of NIS 5,000 (5,000 ש"ח) or more before VAT requires an allocation number (mispar haktzaa) from the Tax Authority platform, and without one the buyer cannot offset the VAT on that expense. The threshold was NIS 10,000 from 1 January 2026.
claims.raw_snippet: החל מיום 1.6.2026 תורחב החובה לקבל מספר הקצאה לחשבונית מס, כך שתחול על עסקאות שסכומן עולה על 5,000 ש"ח

claims.claim: The allocation-number regime began in May 2024. The threshold schedule before VAT is NIS 25,000 from May 2024, NIS 20,000 from January 2025, NIS 10,000 from January 2026, and NIS 5,000 from June 2026.
Independent corroboration of the same four-step schedule from the start of the reform in May 2024.
The Israel Invoices model came into force in May 2024, so transactions dated before that never required an allocation number.
claims.raw_snippet: מת חשבוניות ישראל, נכנסה לתוקף במאי 2024

claims.claim: Section 38(a1) of the VAT Law disallows the input-VAT deduction on a tax invoice whose amount before tax EXCEEDS NIS 5,000 (NIS 10,000 from January 2026 to May 2026) and which carries no number allocated by the Director. There is no buyer-request condition.
claims.raw_snippet: לא יותר ניכוי מס התשומות הכלול בחשבונית מס שסכומה, בלא המס, עולה על 5,000 שקלים חדשים (מינואר 2026 ועד מאי 2026: 10,000 שקלים חדשים) ושאינה כוללת מספר שהקצה לה המנהל

claims.claim: Section 47(a2)(1) applies only to a tax invoice issued for a transaction whose tax is not at the zero rate, so a zero-rated or exempt-only invoice is outside the allocation-number requirement.
